articles.title: Para proteger menores, governo pede fiscalização de seis jogos com riscos semelhantes aos das bets | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedido está relacionado aos seis meses de vigência da ECA Digital, lei que protege crianças e adolescentes na internet e restringiu o acesso de menores a mecanismos de recompensa aleatória em jogos eletrônicos.
articles.summary: Pedido está relacionado aos seis meses de vigência da ECA Digital, lei que protege crianças e adolescentes na internet e restringiu o acesso de menores a mecanismos de recompensa aleatória em jogos eletrônicos.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Justiça pediu à Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD), por meio de nota técnica, uma investigação sobre seis jogos que contêm as chamadas caixas de recompensa (loot boxes) por exporem crianças e adolescentes a riscos semelhantes aos das apostas online — proibidas no Brasil.

O pedido está relacionado aos seis meses de vigência do ECA Digital, lei que protege crianças e adolescentes na internet , e proibiu o acesso de menores a mecanismos de recompensa aleatória em jogos eletrônicos.

NBA 2K26 e WWE 2K26, da Take-Two Interactive; Counter-Strike 2, da Valve; Call of Duty, da Activision; Genshin Impact, da HoYoverse; e PUBG Mobile, da Tencent Games.

Segundo a nota, esses jogos mantêm as caixas de recompensa e têm classificação indicativa de 18 anos, mas não implementaram mecanismos de verificação de idade para impedir o acesso de crianças e adolescentes.

🔎 As caixas de recompensa permitem aos jogadores comprarem, por pagamento direto ou moeda virtual, itens virtuais ou vantagens cujo conteúdo é definido de forma aleatória.

O levantamento é preliminar e, segundo a nota, não permite concluir, por si só, que as empresas estejam descumprindo o ECA Digital. Caberá à fiscalização verificar a situação de cada jogo.

De acordo com relatório da Coordenação-Geral de Políticas de Classificação Indicativa, do Ministério da Justiça, o elemento central do mecanismo é a incerteza: o jogador paga antes de saber o que receberá, e o resultado é sorteado segundo probabilidades definidas pelo próprio fornecedor do jogo.

É a combinação de pagamento, sorte e expectativa de recompensa que, segundo o Ministério da Justiça, aproxima o funcionamento desses mecanismos ao das apostas, como as bet.

"A análise indica que a exposição às caixas de recompensa na infância e adolescência está associada, segundo a literatura científica examinada, a desfechos ligados ao jogo problemático, sofrimento psicológico e danos financeiros, embora essa associação não autorize, isoladamente, afirmar relação causal direta com transtornos clínicos", diz a nota do Ministério da Justiça.

Segundo o documento, esse tipo de funcionamento pode incentivar compras repetidas, já que o jogador não sabe quantas tentativas serão necessárias para conseguir determinada recompensa e pode continuar gastando dinheiro nessa expectativa.

A nota também pede que as informações sejam enviadas ao Ministério da Saúde para subsidiar estudos sobre os impactos das caixas de recompensa na saúde mental de crianças e adolescentes

"Vale destacar que a associação entre a compra de caixas de recompensa por crianças e adolescentes e comportamento problemático de apostas não decorre apenas de um estudo isolado, mas um conjunto de estudo, que atravessa países", acrescenta o governo.

Caberá à ANPD analisar as informações apresentadas pelo Ministério da Justiça e decidir sobre a eventual adoção de medidas.

O levantamento não é definitivo, e outros jogos ainda podem ser incluídos na lista.

articles.title: Fluidez Digital: o segredo das empresas que crescem com tecnologia | G1
articles.standfirst: A fluidez é o ponto de virada. Entenda como alinhar sistemas, processos e pessoas para superar problemas e potencializar o seu negócio.
articles.summary: A fluidez é o ponto de virada. Entenda como alinhar sistemas, processos e pessoas para superar problemas e potencializar o seu negócio.
articles.body:
Na sua empresa, a tecnologia facilita o trabalho ou cria novos gargalos? Fluidez digital é o estágio de maturidade em que os sistemas estão tão integrados e eficientes que a TI deixa de ser uma dor de cabeça e passa a ser impulsionadora de negócio.

A TI pode ser simples e deve ser estratégica

O C-level não precisa se afogar na complexidade técnica para tomar boas decisões. O papel de uma TI madura é justamente traduzir essa complexidade em informações claras, que qualquer diretor consiga entender e usar. Quando a tecnologia flui dessa forma, a empresa ganha a base que precisa para escalar de forma rápida e segura.

Muito além do suporte: a antecipação de problemas

Empresas fluidas não esperam o problema acontecer para agir. Com monitoramento inteligente e análise de dados, incluindo inteligência artificial, a TI passa a atuar de forma proativa, antecipando falhas, identificando vulnerabilidades e propondo melhorias na infraestrutura antes que a diretoria sequer perceba algum impacto na operação.

Os quatro pilares de um parceiro de confiança

O mercado exige um padrão de TI que combine quatro características. Ser próxima, para entender de fato a dor do negócio. Ser técnica, com atualização constante e autoridade sobre o assunto. Ser estratégica, focada em impacto financeiro e não apenas em execução. E ser flexível, adaptando processos à realidade de cada cliente em vez de empurrar soluções padronizadas.

A gente faz a sua transformação digital, você faz o seu negócio crescer. Com mais de 18 anos de experiência e mais de 300 clientes satisfeitos, a Pellissari acredita que a TI deve ser simples e estratégica. Seja organizando processos internos, estruturando a gestão de ativos ou construindo painéis de indicadores, a Pellissari é a base estratégica que empresas de todos os portes usam para construir um ambiente estável e inovador.

Quando a tecnologia flui, o seu negócio decola.

articles.title: Dólar opera em alta, com foco em inflação americana e pesquisas eleitorais; Ibovespa cai | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana avançou 0,17%, cotada a R$ 5,0283. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 0,18%, aos 206.506 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana avançou 0,17%, cotada a R$ 5,0283. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 0,18%, aos 206.506 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar opera em alta nesta quinta-feira (15), com um avanço de 0,42% perto das 13h15, cotado a R$ 5,0492 . Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, tinha queda de 0,28% no mesmo horário, aos 205.936 pontos .

O cenário político brasileiro segue sob os holofotes, conforme investidores repercutem novas pesquisas eleitorais e a aprovação da PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1. Indicadores econômicos no Brasil e nos Estados Unidos também ficam no radar.

▶️ No Brasil, o tema do dia é a aprovação da PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1. A proposta foi aprovada pelo Senado na última quarta-feira por 75 votos a favor e um contra nos dois turnos de votação. Com a aprovação, a emenda constitucional é promulgada pela Mesa do Congresso e a expectativa é que as mudanças aconteçam de forma gradativa.

▶️ No quadro eleitoral, Flávio Bolsonaro apareceu com 46% das intenções de voto no 2º turno, contra 44% de Lula. Os dados são da nova pesquisa Quaest, divulgada na véspera. Nesta quinta-feira, um novo levantamento deve ser divulgado pelo Datafolha. Acompanhe as pesquisas eleitorais no g1.

▶️ Na agenda econômica, o destaque fica com o índice de preços ao produtor (PPI) dos Estados Unidos. O indicador subiu 1,3% em setembro, no maior avanço em mais de quatro anos, em meio à alta dos custos de bens e serviços.

🔎 Os dados reforçam a expectativa de que o Fed possa elevar os juros no fim deste mês. Taxas mais altas nos EUA tendem a fortalecer o dólar e a afastar investidores de mercados emergentes, como o Brasil, além de aumentar a pressão para manter os juros elevados por aqui.

▶️ No Brasil, o foco fica com a Pesquisa Mensal do Comércio (PMC) de agosto. As vendas no varejo subiram 0,1% em agosto sobre julho na série com ajuste sazonal, abaixo do esperado pelo mercado, que previam alta de 0,7%, segundo a Reuters. O resultado acompanha dados mais fracos da indústria e de serviços e confirma a desaceleração da atividade econômica brasileira.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

Flávio Bolsonaro segue em vantagem no 2º turno, diz pesquisa

A primeira pesquisa Quaest do segundo turno, divulgada nesta quarta-feira (14), mostra Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) com 46% das intenções de voto, contra 44% de Lula. Os dois estão em empate técnico dentro da margem de erro, que é de dois pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos.

O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e pelo jornal O Globo. Veja os números:

A Quaest ainda divulgou uma pesquisa sobre a aprovação do governo Lula, mostrando que 48% desaprovam a gestão do petista , enquanto 45% aprovam.

Outro levantamento mostrou, ainda, que 43% dos brasileiros têm medo da volta da família Bolsonaro com a possível vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), ao mesmo tempo em que outros 43% têm medo da reeleição de Lula (PT).

Em relação à última edição da pesquisa, de 3 de outubro, às vésperas do primeiro turno, houve um aumento de 3% nas respostas que citam o medo do retorno da família Bolsonaro. No levantamento anterior, o percentual foi de 40%, menor patamar desde 5 de agosto. Já os participantes que disseram ter mais medo da reeleição de Lula se mantiveram estáveis (43%) desde 21 de setembro.

A expectativa, agora, é pela nova pesquisa do Datafolha, que deve ser divulgada nesta quinta-feira.

A Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que prevê o fim da escala 6x1, com dois dias de descanso remunerado por semana, foi aprovada pelo Senado nesta quarta-feira (14).

A proposta foi aprovada por 75 votos a favor e um contra nos dois turnos de votação. O senador Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS) foi o único a votar contrário à proposta.

Com a aprovação, a emenda constitucional é promulgada pela Mesa do Congresso, sem precisar passar pela sanção do presidente da República, como ocorre com projetos de lei. Ela começa a produzir efeitos após a publicação no Diário Oficial.

Como o g1 mostrou , a expectativa é que as mudanças comecem a valer dois meses após a publicação da emenda constitucional. A partir desse prazo, os trabalhadores passariam a ter direito a dois dias de repouso semanal remunerado, com possibilidade de compensação prevista em norma coletiva, desde que fosse assegurada a média de dois dias de descanso por semana.

A proposta também prevê a redução gradual da jornada semanal, sem diminuição salarial. Durante o primeiro ano de transição, o limite será de 42 horas semanais. Depois desse período, a jornada máxima passará a ser de 40 horas.

Em Wall Street , os principais índices acionários americanos operavam mistos nesta quinta-feira, conforme investidores repercutiam os novos dados de inflação e atividade no país.

Perto das 13h15, o Dow Jones tinha alta de 0,80%, enquanto o S&P 500 subia 0,06% e o Nasdaq Composite caía 0,32%.

O tom ameno também era visto na Europa . No mesmo horário, o DAX , da Alemanha, tinha alta de 0,33%, enquanto o CAC-40 , da França, subia 0,78% e o FTSE 100 , do Reino Unido, ganhava 1,08%.

Na Ásia , as ações chinesas fecharam no menor patamar em 14 meses, acompanhando a fraqueza generalizada nos mercados globais e em meio à queda dos papéis do setor de tecnologia.

O SSEC , índice de Xangai, e o CSI300 , índice que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em Xangai e Shenzen, caíram 1,6%. Entre os demais índices da região, o Nikkei , do Japão, perdeu 4,90% e o Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, desvalorizou 1,03%. O Kospi , da Coreia do Sul, teve perdas de 7,57%.

articles.title: Hackathon do Siará Tech Summit premia soluções para desafio do Banco do Nordeste | G1
articles.standfirst: Três equipes dividiram R$ 10 mil em prêmios após três dias de desenvolvimento de soluções voltadas à análise de projetos da Lei do Bem
articles.summary: Três equipes dividiram R$ 10 mil em prêmios após três dias de desenvolvimento de soluções voltadas à análise de projetos da Lei do Bem
articles.body:
Vencedores do Hackathon do Siará Tech Summit 2026 — Foto: Sebrae/CE

Após três dias de desenvolvimento, mentorias e testes, o Hackathon do Siará Tech Summit chegou ao fim, nesta sexta-feira (9), com a premiação das soluções que mais se destacaram no desafio proposto pelo Banco do Nordeste, por meio do Hubine, seu hub de inovação.

O primeiro lugar ficou com a Equipe 3 – JustIA, que recebeu R$ 5 mil. Em segundo lugar, a Equipe 10 – BnBem levou R$ 3 mil, enquanto a Equipe 13 – Lastro conquistou a terceira colocação e recebeu R$ 2 mil. Também receberam menção honrosa a Equipe 4 – Lastro, com um sistema de apoio à decisão para elegibilidade na Lei do Bem, e a Equipe 24 – Nexo P&D.

O desafio mobilizou participantes de diferentes áreas para desenvolver soluções capazes de apoiar a análise de projetos relacionados à Lei do Bem, combinando conhecimentos de tecnologia, negócios, inovação e outras áreas em equipes multidisciplinares.

Para Alexandre Cavalcante, gerente do Hubine, o processo vai além do resultado final. “A gente está sempre junto do Sebrae para fomentar a inovação e queria parabenizar as equipes que passaram pelo Hackathon. Independentemente de quem ganhou, entendemos que todos são vitoriosos. E gostaria de reforçar que o Hubine está à disposição para continuar essa interação, por entender a importância da inovação no nosso mercado”, afirmou.

Já a gerente da Unidade de Eventos do Sebrae Ceará, Alice Mesquita, destacou a participação de pessoas de diferentes regiões do Estado. “Para a gente do Sebrae é uma enorme satisfação ver que estamos contribuindo com esse ecossistema. Temos representantes de todos os cantos do Ceará e perceber essa participação e descentralização do cenário de inovação é algo fantástico. Todo esse processo é conhecimento que está sendo gerado”, ressaltou.

A premiação encerrou uma jornada marcada pela construção coletiva, troca com mentores e desenvolvimento de soluções para um problema real, reforçando o papel do Hackathon como espaço de formação, conexão e estímulo a novos projetos dentro do Siará Tech Summit .

articles.title: Russia begins diesel exports after Trump deal amid global oil market concerns
articles.summary: Russian diesel has begun reaching global markets following an agreement with US President Donald Trump, the Kremlin said on Thursday, adding that the
articles.body: Russian diesel has begun reaching global markets following an agreement with US President Donald Trump, the Kremlin said on Thursday, adding that the supplies could help stabilise oil markets but would not be sufficient to fully achieve that goal."The diesel has started reaching global markets and is expected to have a positive effect on stabilising oil markets, although it will not be enough to fully stabilize them," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, according to Reuters.Trump said last week that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets to help lower fuel prices. Moscow subsequently partially lifted its ban on diesel exports from October 10 following the agreement.Russian diesel shipments resumeData from financial information provider LSEG showed on Wednesday that Russia had resumed diesel export loadings from the Baltic port of Primorsk.According to the shipping data cited by Reuters, a tanker carrying around 40,000 metric tonnes of ultra-low sulphur diesel was loaded on October 13 and was heading towards Morocco.Trump said on Friday that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel to US and global markets. He also said another 500,000 tonnes would be supplied in November, followed by a further 1 million tonnes "immediately thereafter".However, the initial volume would amount to less than a day's supply for the US transport sector alone.US Energy Information Administration data puts daily consumption in the sector at around 2.94 million barrels. The additional volumes announced by Trump would amount to less than four days of demand for US transport.Trump is seeking to bring down US diesel prices ahead of the country's midterm elections on November 3.Ukraine, European officials criticise dealThe agreement has drawn strong criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, European officials and some Republican politicians in Trump's own party.Russia, meanwhile, has rejected European criticism of the diesel arrangement as "cynical", arguing that European countries continue to purchase some Russian oil and liquefied natural gas.The deal comes amid tensions over efforts to secure an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.Kremlin accuses Kyiv of undermining peace effortsSeparately, the Kremlin said on Thursday that Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries were running counter to US efforts to initiate peace talks, following a drone attack on a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region overnight.Peskov said Moscow did not believe Kyiv had complied with the energy ceasefire announced by Trump on Sunday. Ukraine had said it paused strikes on Russian oil refineries for three days but resumed them after Russia continued attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure."The Ukrainian regime in Kyiv continues to strike these facilities, thereby, of course, coming into serious contradiction with the peace efforts of the United States and of the American negotiators who are indeed making very vigorous efforts to somehow initiate the peace process. But so far, these vigorous attempts have been thwarted by the unwillingness of the Kyiv regime – and of (President Volodymyr) Zelenskyy personally – to make peace," Peskov said.The news agency Associated Press (AP) reported that the drone strike started a fire at the Ryazan refinery, around 300 kilometres southeast of Moscow. A senior Ukrainian official confirmed that Ukraine had hit the facility, while Russia's Defence Ministry and regional governor reported the attack.Russia had previously said the scope of the energy ceasefire had not been defined. On Wednesday, it said it had struck seven Ukrainian energy infrastructure facilities, according to Reuters.The competing claims over compliance with the ceasefire could not be independently verified.Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said Russia had launched more than 850 drones at Ukraine between midnight and Thursday morning.Ukraine's Emergency Services said three people were killed and six injured in a Russian drone attack on the central Kirovohrad region, while the Ukrainian Air Force said its air defences had intercepted 536 Russian drones during the overnight assault.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Mumbai: The Securities and exchange board of India (SEBI) plans to facilitate the sharing of additional information fields relating to mutual funds and
articles.body: Mumbai: The Securities and exchange board of India (SEBI) plans to facilitate the sharing of additional information fields relating to mutual funds and securities holdings on the electronic consolidated account statement (eCAS), Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced on Thursday.Addressing the samvaad 2026 conference on the Accoung aggregator framework organised by Sahamati, Pandey outlined a series of forward-looking regulatory priorities centered on expanding the Account aggregator (AA) framework, bridging capital market holdings with banking assets, improving system-wide interoperability, and tightening data security safeguards.A central highlight of the address was the capital markets regulator’s drive to make portfolio tracking far more comprehensive for retail investors.Currently, eCAS aggregates an investor’s demat holdings and mutual fund units across depositories and asset management companies. SEBI is now actively working to bring traditional banking assets under the same single-window umbrella through the AA network."SEBI is working to facilitate the inclusion of bank deposit information in the electronic consolidated account statement through the AA framework, giving investors a more comprehensive view of their financial assets," Pandey stated.Alongside bank deposits, the regulator intends to deepen the granular data shared on existing investment avenues. Pandey noted that the market watchdog is "working to facilitate the sharing of additional information fields relating to mutual funds and securities holdings, subject to appropriate consent and safeguards."Addressing cross-platform friction in the consent-based data ecosystem, Pandey threw SEBI's weight behind account aggregator interoperability, welcoming the Reserve Bank of India’s recent announcement on the matter.Under the current architecture, data access can often be restricted by bilateral tie-ups between specific Financial information providers (FIPs) and individual account aggregators. Interoperability is expected to dismantle these silos."Once implemented, interoperability would allow investors to share financial information more seamlessly, without being constrained by contractual relationships between a particular financial information provider and an account aggregator," Pandey said.While SEBI is engaging with industry alliance sahamati and market participants to drive broader adoption of the AA mechanism, Pandey stressed that expansion must not come at the cost of investor protection."As the ecosystem expands, the focus must increasingly shift to data quality, reliability, security, meaningful consent, grievance redressal, and accountability," Pandey emphasized, pointing out that sahamati, in its capacity as a self-regulatory organization (SRO), can play an instrumental role in standardizing technical and operational protocols across the board.The regulator believes a fully integrated financial view will serve as a foundation for broader market benefits, enabling "more holistic investment advice, better financial planning, more informed investment decisions, and improved investor services."You use AI every day. articles.title: Rs 1 crore-plus salaries: Amid layoffs, which Indian IT sector jobs are getting huge salary premiums?
articles.summary: Till a few years ago, software engineers in India were commanding high salary premiums and the IT sector was a reliable source of employment.
articles.body: Till a few years ago, software engineers in India were commanding high salary premiums and the IT sector was a reliable source of employment. While still employing lakhs, the artificial intelligence-led disruptions have meant that there is growing uncertainty on the relevance of traditional IT sector roles.As Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital says, “Every few years, the labour market crosses a threshold that is easy to miss in the moment and impossible to reverse in hindsight. India's digital workforce crossed one this year.”“This landscape brings immense opportunity, but it also collapses old certainties about how talent is valued. Job titles and role definitions are becoming less reliable indicators of capability or compensation,” she says.Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior. Which roles are in demand? What are the average salary levels for special capability sets and which roles are under pressure?What are the salary levels for those getting hired at premiums?The fundamental point to understand is that India’s technology talent market is witnessing a shift towards skill-differentiated compensation; with specialised capabilities in AI, machine learning, cloud engineering and data science becoming increasingly valuable.According to a TeamLease Digital report on Digital Skills and Salary Primer FY2026-27, there is a widening pay gap in India’s technology sector, with premiums increasingly going to professionals who can build, integrate, secure and manage AI systems. Routine, execution-led roles are facing greater salary pressure, while specialised skills are becoming more valuable.The premium concentrates in four families, AI, Data, Cloud and Cybersecurity, and peaks where capability depth meets governance and scale.And, this divide is visible across AI skill tiers. For example, the report puts entry-level median pay for AI-core roles at Rs 13.2 lakh, compared with Rs 9-10.2 lakh for AI-adjacent roles and Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh for AI-support roles. The projected salary growth is 16-21% for AI-core, against 13-18% for AI-adjacent and 7-8% for AI-support.Not only that, the premiums also extend to architecture, data and cybersecurity. The report says that skills such as GenAI engineers, AI architects, ML platform and cloud security are the highest in demand.The report lists annual salaries of Rs 1.08 crore for AI Architects, Rs 1.02 crore for Industrial Data Architects and Rs 95.8 lakh for OT Security Architects. These figures reflect the value that is being placed on designing, securing and governing complex technology systems, beyond coding alone.“The 108.6 LPA figure is the median for AI Architects with 15+ years in our analysis of 37,000 roles. It reflects a senior role, not a market-wide norm. The differentiator is the ability to own architecture, scale production systems, manage risk, and connect technical decisions to business outcomes,” explains Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital.Also, geographies no longer define premiums as much. For example, according to the report, a GenAI engineer in Indore earns around Rs 16.5 lakh per annum, and out-earns cybersecurity talent in Bengaluru that gets Rs 14.4 lakh.Milind Shah, Managing Director, Randstad Digital - India tells TOI that the compensation for niche AI roles can vary considerably depending on the depth of expertise, role complexity and business impact. On an average, talent with niche tech skills may command anywhere between a 10-25% premium.Why are these roles commanding a premium? It’s a mix of skill shortage and the roles themselves generating more business value that routine IT jobs no longer are.According to Neeti Sharma, only about 16% of India’s IT professionals hold AI skills, so the supply is thin. She explains that companies are not able to find people who can take AI from pilot to production and stand accountable for it.“But this is not wage inflation. The market is pricing roles whose output is the AI system itself, which makes them the hardest to substitute. Routine support keeps operations running, and that is the layer AI is compressing first. Employers are paying for scarcity, and for people who can own the outcome,” she tells TOI.So, what can IT sector professionals do?Reskilling is central to the shift. The TeamLease report points to pathways such as moving testers into intelligent operations, analysts into decision intelligence, and mid-career professionals into platform, product, governance and architecture roles.Its broader message is that combining core technical expertise with AI skills, domain knowledge and business judgement will increasingly determine salary growth.Milind Shah shares strategies for every level:At the entry level, he says professionals with strong foundations in software engineering, data and AI application can distinguish themselves through practical implementation skills. At the mid-career level, expertise in areas such as AI engineering, machine learning operations and enterprise AI integration becomes particularly valuable as organisations look to move beyond experimentation towards deployment at scale. At the senior level, compensation increasingly reflects the ability to architect enterprise AI systems, lead transformation programmes and ensure that technology investments deliver measurable business outcomes, he adds.Biggest takeawaySo, what does this mean for tech professionals? The biggest takeaway is that professionals need to shift from being defined by the roles they perform to the capabilities they bring to the business.“As AI becomes embedded across technology functions, the value of talent will increasingly depend on the ability to adapt, solve complex problems and apply emerging technologies to real-world business challenges,” Milind Shah says.For early-career professionals, this means building strong technical fundamentals while gaining hands-on experience in AI, data and cloud technologies. For mid-career professionals, the priority is to move beyond execution and develop the ability to integrate technologies, improve workflows and translate domain expertise into scalable solutions. For senior professionals, the focus must extend to strategic decision-making, enterprise-wide AI adoption, governance and the ability to connect technology investments with business performance, he says.For people who are in traditional IT sector roles, it’s important to understand that while the jobs are not disappearing, routine execution roles are reducing.Repetitive reporting, manual testing, basic operational support and rule-based processing face pressure as AI and automation reshape work. The report does not suggest that all these jobs will disappear; rather, salary growth may slow unless workers move towards higher-value responsibilities.“Those in repetitive reporting, manual testing, and basic support are most exposed. The route up is adjacency, not reinvention: a BI analyst into data engineering, a sysadmin into cloud, a QA or IAM specialist into security and governance. Pair one technical skill with deep sector knowledge, and keep proof of work that moves a business outcome,” Neeti Sharma says.Not only that, this shift also has implications for how professionals approach career development.So if you are planning to upskill to keep yourself relevant, understand that it should not be driven solely by the popularity of a technology or the prospect of a higher salary.“Instead, employees should identify the capabilities emerging as critical within their industry, understand how these capabilities address business needs and build demonstrable expertise through practical application,” Milind Shah advises.You use AI every day. articles.title: Wall Street is 'tiring of the Bank of Nvidia, the Bank of AMD and the Bank of Broadcom': Baird's Mortonson
articles.summary: The sell-off in AI-related stocks, according to Baird tech strategist Ted Mortonson, is increasingly about who needs financing and what that financing costs.
articles.body:
The sell-off in AI-related stocks, according to Baird tech strategist Ted Mortonson, is increasingly about who needs financing and what that financing costs.

"I think the street is tiring of the Bank of Nvidia, the Bank of AMD and the Bank of Broadcom," Mortonson told Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Brooke DiPalma (video above), referring to chipmakers Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), and Broadcom ( AVGO ).

"This is very unusual in this cycle… It's not going over well with the institutional community," he added.

Mortonson pointed to "a higher cost of capital" and "a lot of scrutiny now on circular finance," which he said was "coming out of the Anthropic research meeting."

Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) reportedly told investors at a closed meeting that its third-quarter revenue climbed to $16.8 billion.

CoreWeave stock ( CRWV ) fell more than 15% on Wednesday and fell again in pre-market trading on Thursday. Mortonson noted that that CoreWeave, Nebius ( NBIS ), and Oracle ( ORCL ) are "probably at the bottom" of tech on free cash flow.

These companies are "very dependent on financing going forward," he said., adding: "That is the real issue… their free cash flow and the cost of capital [is] so elevated today that anything that has that exposure is being sold."

Adding to the souring sentiment, a new Gartner forecast that most neocloud providers will "cease independent operations" by 2030.

Chipmakers with strong results are getting hit, too.

"Portfolio managers are selling names that have unadulterated blowout numbers, and they're not acting well," Mortonson said, pointing to Samsung ( 005930.KS ), Micron ( MU ), and ASML ( ASML ).

So is the drop a chance to buy? "That's the million dollar question," Mortonson said.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) was up about 87% for the year as of Oct. 6, which he called "a good decade of performance." It closed Wednesday up 65% for that period.

The pullback is "healthy," Mortonson said, but it also "represents that the institutional community that has been very overweight the infrastructure play [and] is going elsewhere."

Where? "They're probably going to software, to be honest with you."

Some money is leaving tech altogether, he added, as a lot of portfolio managers "are trying to lock in performance as they go into the end of the year."

articles.title: Wholesale inflation surged in September, keeping affordability in focus ahead of the midterms
articles.summary: US wholesale inflation jumped in September to its highest level in more than four years, marking the second hotter-than-expected inflation reading this week and adding to concerns about the economy just weeks before the midterm elections.
articles.body: US wholesale inflation jumped in September to its highest level in more than four years, marking the second hotter-than-expected inflation reading this week and adding to concerns about the economy just weeks before the midterm elections. The Producer Price Index rose 1.3% from the month before and 6.3% from the year before, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data released Thursday morning. It’s a sharp upswing from August when wholesale prices rose 0.5% to an annual rate of 5.6%. The latest PPI landed a day after September’s Consumer Price Index report, which similarly showed that inflationary pressures were broadening. Sharply rising gas prices lifted the overall CPI to a 3.7% annual rate; but excluding gas and food, a closely watched gauge of underlying inflation heated up to 2.6% from 2.4%, underscoring that a variety of categories are experiencing price pressures. The reports of accelerating price hikes come just weeks before the midterms, where affordability – or lack thereof – is expected to factor in heavily for US voters. Economists had expected September PPI to increase 0.5% from August and 5.3% annually, according to FactSet. Instead, September marked the fastest monthly increase since March 2022 and the highest annual rate since December 2022, the year when US inflation hit a 40-year high. Energy prices, driven higher by geopolitical conflicts including the war with Iran, drove September’s increase, accounting for 80% of the 2.9% leap in goods prices. That’s the largest-ever monthly increase, according to BLS data that goes back to 2009. However, businesses are contending with price pressures beyond energy. Core PPI, which strips out food and energy, rose at 0.7%, its fastest rate in five months, lifting the annual rate to 5%, its highest since January 2023. High energy prices spread A collection of fuel-sensitive transportation-related categories, including airfares, were largely behind the lift in core wholesale inflation, said Oliver Allen, senior US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics. Services-related price hikes were more muted as well when stripping out transportation, warehousing and trade services (a category that measures margins for retailers and wholesalers), he added. “I don’t think the details are as ugly as the topline headline and core numbers suggest,” he said. “But they’re still not great.” Higher energy prices are still working their way through the economy, he added. Prices for finished consumer goods (excluding food and energy), which rose 0.2% from August, are expected to continue climbing in the coming months, he said. PPI, which measures the average change in prices received by producers of goods and services, serves as a potential bellwether for what consumers could experience in the months to come. Some of the PPI data also feeds in to the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, which is what the Federal Reserve uses for its 2% target rate. If policymakers were looking for evidence of persistent inflation, the September CPI and PPI have presented it, said Joe Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM US. He expects that PCE, due later this month, will do so as well. More importantly for the consumer, the energy shock that caused an increase in transportation costs is starting to show up in food prices, he said, noting fresh and dry vegetable prices were up 41%, grains were up 17.4% and oilseeds were up 11.4% from August. Gas purchases pump up retail sales A separate report from the Commerce Department Thursday showed that Americans slowed their spending in September. US retail sales slowed to 0.8% last month after posting a surprisingly strong 1.3% gain in August, according to the latest monthly report from the Commerce Department. However, when excluding purchases at gas stations, retail sales rose just 0.2%. Retail sales data is adjusted for seasonality but not inflation: When factoring in the pace of monthly price hikes (which rose at an unpalatable 0.6% in September), last month’s retail sales fell even flatter. “Higher gas prices are beginning to bite because, unlike earlier in the year, there’s no offset this time around from fiscal policy,” Michael Pearce, chief US economist at Oxford Economics, wrote in a note to investors Thursday. “We estimate the cumulative additional spend on gasoline so far this year now outweighs the rise in tax refunds from a year ago.” On an annual basis, retail sales were up 6.3% (4.5%, excluding gas station spending). However, on a three-month annualized basis, that growth rate is running at 2.4%, signaling a loss of momentum heading into the holiday shopping season, noted Gary Schlossberg, global strategist at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. Treasury yields were lower despite the hot inflation report as investors unnerved by a drop in AI stocks flocked into the safety of bonds. Major stock indexes were mixed: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell 0.3% and 0.9%, respectively. The Dow, meanwhile, rose 0.6%.

articles.title: RBI cautions regulated entities against monetising data
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI has cautioned all regulated entities against monetising customer data and stressed the need to preserve neutrality in the consent-based
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI has cautioned all regulated entities against monetising customer data and stressed the need to preserve neutrality in the consent-based data-sharing framework, while outlining plans to improve interoperability, standardise data formats and expand access to financial information.Speaking at Samvaad 2026, organised by sahamati, the self-regulatory organisation for the AA ecosystem, RBI executive director Kesavan Ramachandran said data must be shared only with customer consent and strictly for the purpose authorised. “When we have a lot of data at our disposal, there is always a tendency, at least in the minds of unscrupulous users of data, to monetise it,” he said, adding that the ecosystem “will and must always guard against the monetization of data.”Ramachandran said financial data must be shared only to the extent explicitly requested and approved by customers, in line with the digital personal data protection act. AAs must preserve the framework's data-blind architecture by not storing or decrypting customer information or transmitting it without verifiable consent. Misuse or unauthorised exposure of data could undermine the ecosystem's credibility.He also cautioned financial information providers (FIPs) against withholding data when customers have given valid consent. As artificial intelligence gains ground in financial services, institutions must adopt the technology prudently and guard against security breaches.RBI is working towards full interoperability across the AA network, following the roadmap announced by the RBI Governor, Ramachandran said. Standardised technical systems would allow customers and financial information users (FIUs) to exchange information seamlessly across platforms, enabling smaller AAs to compete with larger players.He described the AA framework as the fourth pillar of India's digital public infrastructure, alongside Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM), the unified payments interface (UPI) and the unified lending interface (ULI). Together, these systems are expected to widen credit access, particularly for first-time and underserved borrowers.Depositories are also being enabled to offer customers a consolidated view of their demat and financial holdings, expanding the information available through AA integrations.Sahamati will work with reserve bank information technology (ReBIT) to standardise data formats across more than 19 financial information categories currently active in the ecosystem. This is intended to make information exchanged between FIPs and FIUs uniform, readable and usable.Ramachandran called for greater reciprocity among financial institutions, saying entities that access data as FIUs should also participate as FIPs to supply information. This would promote more balanced data sharing across banks, NBFCs and fintech companies.He said regulators and industry participants must work together to resolve operational challenges and preserve customer trust, in keeping with the consent-based principle underlying sahamati's name.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sylvester Stallone sold the 'Rocky' rights in 1976 — 50 years later, he's done fighting for them
articles.summary: Movie icon Sylvester Stallone is done trying to get the rights back to his life-changing “Rocky” franchise.
articles.body:
Listen and subscribe to Power Players with Brian Sozzi on Apple Podcasts , Amazon Music , Spotify , YouTube , or wherever you find your favorite podcasts.

Movie icon Sylvester Stallone is done trying to get the rights back to his life-changing "Rocky" franchise.

"God, I have tried," Stallone said in a new episode of the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast (video above; listen in below).

Stallone famously wrote the screenplay for "Rocky" in three days and demanded he play the lead role. He then sold the rights to producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff. The original deal didn't cut him an equity stake in the franchise, a long-term asset that he could have passed down to his children after his death.

Stallone has been unable to work out a deal for a share in the decades since. The "Rocky" franchise will celebrate its 50th anniversary since its release on Nov. 20, 1976.

"I don't want to get into it, but it was pretty locked up, and there was a lot of maneuvering behind the scenes," Stallone added. "Believe me, I have tried because I have said, wow, it's like, can I visit my child? But you know, time has moved on, and I have been very, very lucky. So I try not to dwell on that because the answer is absolutely not."

There really is no other way to put it: Stallone has earned his spot among Hollywood legends through blood, sweat, and tears. With that success — ranging from big-screen films "Rocky" and "Rambo" to the series "Tulsa King," which returns for its latest season on Friday on streaming platform Paramount+ — has come an equally impressive business backdrop, no matter if he owns the rights to "Rocky."

Recognizing the power of controlling his own IP, Stallone expanded his earnings beyond simple acting fees — which routinely topped $15 million to $20 million per project — by taking on writer, director, and executive producer roles across his iconic "Rocky," "Rambo," and "The Expendables" franchises.

In 2018, Stallone formed his own media operations, founding Balboa Productions, a film and television outfit that has successfully commercialized projects like "Tulsa King" and "Samaritan."

Beyond entertainment, Stallone has invested in other assets such as real estate and watches.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. articles.title: Lord’s Mark Industries Limited acquires Radio Electric Private Limited, combining engineering heritage with new growth opportunities
articles.summary: Bringing the established Radiotone brand and its specialised transformer expertise into its portfolio, Lord’s Mark Industries Limited is expanding its
articles.body: Bringing the established Radiotone brand and its specialised transformer expertise into its portfolio, Lord’s Mark Industries Limited is expanding its presence in electrical manufacturing and engineering. The move adds decades of technical know-how, relationships with leading industrial customers, an established export network and substantial scope for increased manufacturing capacity.Aligned with the company’s Lighting & Energy Division, the move supports Lord’s Mark Industries Limited’s broader ambition to build a diversified, technology-led Indian enterprise. By strengthening established businesses with proven engineering capabilities and creating avenues for future expansion, the company aims to broaden its manufacturing base, tap new market opportunities and drive sustainable, long-term growth.Founded in 1939, Radio Electric Private Limited brings nearly nine decades of engineering and manufacturing heritage, while the Radiotone brand has been established since 1980. The company specialises in variable autotransformers (Variacs) and toroidal transformers, with products largely manufactured to customer-specific requirements. Its portfolio includes three-phase air-cooled Variacs ranging up to 1,000 A, three-phase oil- cooled Variacs ranging up to 2,000 A, double-layer Variacs and tailor-made single-phase toroidal transformers ranging from 30 VA to 20 kVA. The company also manufactures specialised variable transformers, AC power sources, voltage isolation transformers, variable inductors and chokes.Engineering expertise built over decadesA key strength of Radio Electric Private Limited is its specialised design know-how in a niche segment where technical expertise and reliability are critical. The company pioneered its double-layer Variac design in 1979–80, which went on to become widely used by servo stabiliser manufacturers. Its high-current manufacturing capability, particularly in three-phase air- and oil-cooled Variacs, represents a specialised engineering capability that is difficult to replicate quickly.The company has also developed customised solutions for demanding applications. Its isolated double-wound variable transformer, for instance, integrates variable voltage control and isolation into a single transformer configuration, reflecting the company's emphasis on solving specific customer engineering requirements.A strategic acquisition built on proven capabilitiesThe transaction brings together Radio Electric Private Limited’s 87-year manufacturing legacy, the established Radiotone brand, specialised transformer design expertise and high-current manufacturing capabilities with Lord’s Mark Industries Limited’s growth-oriented business platform. The acquisition gives Lord’s Mark Industries Limited access to a profitable, debt-free operating business with established relationships across approximately 40–50 customers, including blue-chip industrial names, repeat export customers across seven international markets, a trained technical workforce and an established vendor ecosystem. With the existing manufacturing facility currently operating at approximately 50% of machine capacity on a single shift, Lord’s Mark Industries Limited also gains significant headroom to scale production without immediate large capital expenditure.A profitable business with significant capacity upsideThe acquisition provides Lord’s Mark Industries Limited with an established operating manufacturing business rather than a greenfield investment. Radio Electric Private Limited has demonstrated consistent profitability, operates as a debt-free business, and brings an established customer base, export presence and proven manufacturing capabilities to Lord’s Mark Industries Limited.The company’s existing manufacturing infrastructure presents significant scope for enhanced capacity utilisation and production expansion through operational efficiencies and the introduction of additional shifts. With the right marketing strategy, improved utilisation and focused business development, the company is well positioned to scale its operations significantly and build a business with the potential to achieve revenues running into hundreds of crores in the coming years.Strong customer relationships and an established export footprintRadio Electric Private Limited has developed a steady customer base of approximately 40–50 businesses, with long-standing relationships including Siemens Limited, Hitachi Hi-Rel Power Electronics Private Limited, Larsen & Toubro Limited, Bharat Bijlee Limited, Aplab Limited, Underwriters Laboratories India Private Limited and Intellux Electronics Private Limited.The company's customer base has been built largely through engineering reputation, referrals and repeat business, creating an opportunity for Lord’s Mark Industries Limited to now complement this organic customer acquisition model with a structured sales and marketing strategy.Radio Electric Private Limited also has repeat export customers across seven countries, including markets in Europe, the United States, Canada, South Africa, Dubai and the Philippines. This existing international base provides Lord’s Mark Industries Limited with a platform to deepen exports and pursue additional opportunities across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Africa.Unlocking the next phase of growthFollowing the acquisition, Lord’s Mark Industries Limited plans to build on Radio Electric Private Limited's established strengths through a more structured domestic and international growth strategy. This includes strengthening the sales organisation, developing dealer networks in key industrial clusters, expanding OEM engagement, participating in relevant industrial exhibitions and enhancing the company's digital presence.The company also sees an opportunity to broaden its customer base beyond servo voltage stabiliser manufacturers to include test and measurement laboratories, educational institutions, research and development centres, electrical original equipment manufacturers and utilities.The existing product portfolio can further be strengthened through potential development of motorised Variacs, variable AC power sources, test benches, isolation and step-up/step-down transformers, digital-metered Variacs and automatic voltage regulation and line-conditioning solutions.From transformer manufacturer to a broader electrical engineering platformThe acquisition also provides Lord’s Mark Industries Limited with a technical platform from which to explore adjacent, higher-value applications. These could include customised toroidal and specialised transformers for medical equipment, audio systems, UPS and inverter applications, solar and energy-storage systems, railways and specialised electronics, alongside inductors, chokes and other engineered transformer solutions.This creates the potential to progressively transform Radio Electric Private Limited from a specialised transformer manufacturer into a broader electrical engineering and power-control solutions platform, while leveraging its existing manufacturing infrastructure, technical expertise and customer relationships.Preserving legacy while accelerating growthLord’s Mark Industries Limited intends to ensure continuity during the transition, with the existing trained team and vendor ecosystem continuing to support operations and production remaining at the existing facility under the lease arrangement. As part of the transition, Mr. Umesh Marathe will be available as a consultant for one year, enabling the systematic transfer and documentation of critical design and process knowledge developed over decades.Commenting on the acquisition, Dr. Sachidanand Upadhyay, MD & CEO, Lord’s Mark Industries Limited, said: “Radio Electric Private Limited represents a rare combination of engineering heritage, specialised technology, customer trust and significant untapped growth potential. What attracted us was not simply the company’s history, but the strength of the underlying business—a profitable manufacturing operation, established blue-chip customer relationships, an export track record and specialised technology refined over decades. Lord’s Mark Industries Limited is committed to building high-end transformer manufacturing capabilities to serve the Indian market as well as international markets. This acquisition gives us a strategic edge in the rapidly growing Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) segment, while also enabling us to develop critical components in-house, creating greater value and improving profitability across our medical device business. We see this acquisition as an opportunity to preserve the strengths that have made Radiotone a trusted name while providing the business with a larger growth platform, stronger market access and a more structured approach to domestic and international expansion. Our objective is to take this established Indian engineering capability into its next phase of growth and build a larger, globally competitive electrical manufacturing business.”The move underscores Lord’s Mark Industries Limited’s commitment to unlocking the potential of established Indian engineering businesses and positioning them for greater scale, competitiveness and growth across domestic and international markets. By bringing Radio Electric Private Limited’s decades of engineering expertise, trusted Radiotone brand, established customer relationships and export capabilities onto a larger growth platform, Lord’s Mark aims to build on a strong manufacturing foundation and unlock new opportunities across the electrical engineering landscape.More than an expansion of its portfolio, this marks a strategic investment in proven Indian engineering capabilities, with the potential to shape Radiotone’s next phase of growth and create lasting value.For more details, visit the website.Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.You use AI every day. articles.title: Inflation hit businesses even harder than consumers last month
articles.summary: Businesses were hit by inflation last month at levels not seen since late 2022.
articles.body: Businesses were hit by inflation last month at levels not seen since late 2022. The latest U.S. wholesale inflation report showed that the prices businesses paid to produce goods in September jumped sharply, to 6.3% on an annual basis. From August, prices overall rose 0.6%, the producer price index report showed. The PPI report is typically seen as a sign of what’s to come for consumer prices, and this one followed a consumer price index report Wednesday that also reflected a jump in prices. Both reports indicate that inflation is back on the rise. But unlike high inflation earlier this year, the current effects of rising prices are distributed broadly across the entire economy — beyond merely those sectors exposed to soaring gas, diesel and jet fuel prices. The consumer and producer price indexes are also the last major inflation readings before voters across the country head to the polls in the midterm elections. At many locations, early voting is already underway. Oil and gas prices have soared ever since the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. “Half of the September increase” in producer prices was from the rising cost of gas, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Thursday. Likewise, prices for “diesel fuel, fresh and dry vegetables, jet fuel, residential electric power, and crude petroleum also rose.” Economists say that the most troubling recent price hikes have been those for diesel. Diesel fuel is critical to powering the farming, transportation and shipping sectors. When diesel prices go up, the knock-on effects of those higher costs can show up in just about every sector of consumer goods. Months of efforts by the Trump administration to bring down prices have failed to make a meaningful dent in rising costs. All of the key numbers in Thursday’s PPI report were far more than had been expected by economists and analysts. The so-called “core” PPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, jumped 0.7% from August. From this time one year ago, it rose 5%. The report reinforced some market expectations that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates sooner than expected, during its Oct. 27-28 meeting. A rate hike would add more pressure on consumers, who are already facing high borrowing costs due to rising bond yields. The average interest rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage Thursday was 7.45%. Bond yields fell sharply Thursday in early trading, although this was primarily because investors were seen as moving money out of interest rate-sensitive tech stocks and into bonds. Tech stocks have become highly sensitive to interest rates in recent years because the top players are spending hundreds of billions of dollars — much of it borrowed with interest — to build data centers around the world.

articles.title: Facing serious headwinds, Air India sharpens cost control focus
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Air India MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam has set up a “multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost savings team” to find all possible ways and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Air India MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam has set up a “multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost savings team” to find all possible ways and means of reducing expenditure “on full-time basis” amid mounting losses. Air India reported a loss of about $2.3 billion in 2025-26, the biggest annual loss since the Tata Group acquired the airline along with AI Express in Jan 2022. Overall, since then the airline has lost about $5.7 billion due to a combination of both internal and external factors.“While many external factors remain beyond our control, how we manage costs is something each of us can influence every day. Cost saving… requires active participation and commitment of every employee… Alongside operational excellence, we need to embed a mindset of frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making in everything we do. We should continually challenge ourselves to ask – is this expenditure necessary? Is there a more efficient way to achieve the same outcome? Small decisions, taken consistently across the organisation, can collectively strengthen our financial resilience,” said Tewolde in his first internal note to employees after recently getting security clearance to take over as Air India CEO.While airlines globally have been facing elevated oil prices since the West Asia crisis along with other geopolitical challenges, Indian carriers have been worse off due to the rupee crashing and Pakistan airspace closure only for them. For Air India, the situation is even worse post the deadly Ahmedabad crash last June. Tata-owned AI’s first CEO Campbell Wilson resigned citing personal reasons and now it is up to the former Ethiopian Airlines CEO to revive the Maharaja.“…a multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost savings team has been established on full-time basis to identify cost-saving opportunities across the organisation. They will systematically review all expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities across functions,” his memo says.“This spirit of unity and collaboration becomes even more important as we navigate an exceptionally challenging operating environment. Ongoing airspace closures, the conflict in the Middle East and its resulting operational disruptions, and persistently high jet fuel costs continue to place significant pressure on airlines across the industry. While these challenges may test us, they also reinforce the importance of standing together, supporting one another, and working collectively toward our shared goals. Our ability to overcome these headwinds will depend not on individual efforts, but on how effectively we come together as one team,” he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: MUMBAI: India should expand the account aggregator (AA) network to cover more than 50% of adults within the next three years and broaden the range of financial data available through it to help small businesses access credit and create jobs amid AI-led disruption, Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani said on Thursday.Speaking at the Samvaad 2026 conference, Nilekani called for integrating new data sources, including income tax returns, provident fund contributions, small savings and FASTag records, over the next 12 to 24 months.A decade after RBI issued its initial master direction on account aggregators in Sept 2016, the ecosystem processes 10 lakh consents and 1.2 crore data transactions daily. This will really be a big thing in the next 2-3 years,” Nilekani said.He said adoption must shift from institutions encouraging customers to use the system to consumers actively seeking it to secure better financial products. “Today it's a push thing. Everybody should say, 'I want to use the AA system to get my data to get a better loan or a better insurance policy or whatever.'”Nilekani said the expansion of small businesses could help offset job losses as AI automates service-sector work and robots take over manufacturing tasks. He argued that small enterprises, where employees handle multiple functions such as logistics, sales and stocking, could be more resilient to automation.Nilekani said small businesses could cushion AI-driven job losses. Enabling 10 million enterprises to hire five people each would create 50 million jobs, which he described as “AI-proof”. India's startup ecosystem has grown from fewer than 10,000 entities in 2016 to over 150,000 and could reach 1 million by 2035, alongside an estimated 16 million micro-enterprises and GST-registered businesses.To widen credit access for small businesses, gig workers and street vendors, he proposed adding income tax returns, EPFO records, post office deposits, self-help group data, FASTag histories and BBPS utility records to the AA network over the next two years. articles.title: As AI stocks plunge, Apple is riding high
articles.summary: Apple is avoiding the worst of the AI sell off.
articles.body:
Apple ( AAPL ) is proving to be a safe port for investors amid a deepening sell-off in AI stocks , driven by fears of hotter-than-anticipated inflation data, neocloud debt loads, and circular investing.

The epicenter of the storm is neocloud company CoreWeave ( CRWV ). The company's stock plummeted 15% on Wednesday and continued to decline Thursday, dropping more than 8% in early trading amid concerns about its ability to cover the debt it's piled up to fund its data center build-out.

Then there's the circular investing conversation.

Questions about circular investing, in which chipmakers like Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ) invest in neocloud companies like CoreWeave only for those neoclouds to use the funding to buy the GPUs from their investors, have stalked the market for months. Periodically reaching a fever pitch before dying down amid strong earnings results from AI firms.

The combination of inflation, debt-heavy balance sheets, and circular investing put pressure on AI stocks across the board, with Nvidia stock falling 6% over the last five days. AMD has taken a 13% hit over the same period, while Intel ( INTC ) is off 14%.

The rout hasn't been contained to the US market, either. South Korea's KOSPI index ( ^KS11 ) is down 18%.

In the midst of the AI sell-off, the iPhone maker's market capitalization crossed the $5 trillion mark . It's the second time Apple has reached the milestone. It initially hit $5 trillion in July, before falling back down into the $4 trillion range.

The move stands in stark contrast to its AI-centric peers. It doesn't hurt that, unlike others in the space, Apple hasn't had to shell out billions building new AI data centers, which has helped insulate it from broader market shocks.

Apple isn't immune to the impact of the AI boom, though. The ongoing global shortage of memory and storage chips pushed the company to raise prices across a variety of products.

Still, that hasn't hurt Apple's sales numbers quite yet. It continues to ride high on strong demand for its iPhone lineup, and is preparing for its foldable iPhone Duo to hit the market on Oct. 23.

Starting at $1,999, the Duo could prove too pricey for most consumers, but if Apple can lure even a small number of customers willing to spend the extra cash on its first foldable, the Duo could boost the consumer tech giant's bottom line.

articles.title: Cracks are beginning to show in the stock market, as doubts grow about AI investments
articles.summary: Just a after hitting fresh all-time highs, U.S. stocks are under strain as investors worry about returns on the trillions of dollars that have been put into AI.
articles.body: Just one week after hitting fresh all-time highs, U.S. stocks are showing signs of strain as investors begin to fret about returns on the trillions of dollars that have been put into AI. For U.S. consumers, it could mean a shakier economy moving forward. As of Thursday morning, the S&P 500 was off more than 1% from its week-ago record, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq had fallen about 4% below its peak last week. Driving the declines: Quarterly revenue growth at Anthropic has slowed, the Financial Times reported Wednesday. The AI giant is expected to be worth more than $1 trillion when it goes public, and at nearly $17 billion, its revenue is still massive and the company said it is profitable. There are also rising concerns about whether China-based memory technology companies could undermine, or even overtake, their Western rivals. And even though the AI data center buildout has created a global shortage of processing chips, there are fears that Chinese mass production of memory chips could flood the market with an oversupply. Meanwhile, investors have begun selling off the bonds backing some data centers, primarily over fears that AI revenues won’t be sufficient to cover the massive sums that have been borrowed to finance the building of the centers. On Thursday, economist Ed Yardeni, a widely respected market commentator, lowered his year-end target for the S&P 500 target to 7,900, down from 8,400, over what he said was rising investor caution about the artificial intelligence trade and lingering doubts about inflation and higher interest rates. The S&P 500 currently sits at about 7,600. Most Americans don’t directly own tech stocks, let alone work in AI, which a growing number of studies show may have begun to limit job opportunities. Still, the AI buildout has been a massive part of what’s bolstering the economy, at least on paper. Nearly half of all U.S. economy growth this year is attributable to tech-related spending. Those investments have also lifted the stock market even as a growing swath of other companies have experienced sharp declines in their share prices. The tech-driven gains have in turn created a wealth effect that has helped propel steady U.S. consumer spending and, by extension, the job market. The result has been sturdy economic growth, even as lower-income and even middle-income households have continued to struggle under stubborn inflation and declining earnings. “While higher interest rates, higher oil prices and persistent inflation create risks to the economy, strong positive forces such as the investment in AI infrastructure, high employment levels and consistent wage growth continue to outweigh the risks,” Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf said earlier this week. But other economists say consumers are already contending with a host of stressors that stand to weaken their position. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Thursday that inflation among businesses reached its highest rate since December 2022 — price growth that could eventually trickle down to consumers. If tech spending — and stocks — show any sign of sustained declines, broader U.S. economic growth would likely be at risk. “Higher interest rates, elevated energy prices, slow job growth and the sell-off in equities (if it continues) are all downside risks to consumer spending,” analysts with Citi wrote in a note Thursday.

articles.title: Will SpaceX merge with Tesla? Speculation resurfaces it could happen before the end of 2026
articles.summary: The steady drip of Tesla - SpaceX merger talk is increasing, and this time it's coming from a Wall Street bank.
articles.body:
The steady drip of Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) merger talk is increasing, and this time it's coming from a Wall Street bank.

In a note to clients on Wednesday, Barclays analyst Dan Levy said a tie-up "has increasingly become the consensus expectation." He pointed to media reports and to Elon Musk's own public hints. For now, though, it's still speculation.

Tesla and SpaceX stock were both lower in Thursday's trade, along with the broader tech sector.

Timing was the most notable part of Levy's note. Tesla must hold its annual general meeting [AGM] by Dec. 6, per SEC rules, and Levy and Barclays believe that this would be the appropriate avenue for shareholders to vote on a proposal.

Levy said a merger announcement that slips later into October or early November "may increasingly challenge merger approval as part of the AGM." In that case, a deal wouldn't be dead, but may come instead in the next six to 12 months, since investors see an advantage in closing any deal under the Trump administration's friendly M&A environment.

Levy argues AI vertical integration would be a key component of the merger. Tesla's physical AI, such as Robotaxi and Optimus, would be paired with SpaceX's virtual AI, such as Grok, all supplied by the companies' planned Terafab chip plant. Right now, Terafab decisions need approval from both boards, a process Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has said would take "a while."

Musk's shareholding in the two companies illustrates how a merger would unfold.

Musk owns around 20% of Tesla, compared with about 48% of SpaceX. SpaceX super-voting Class B shares give him around 82% of the vote. SpaceX is worth about $2.1 trillion and Tesla about $1.5 trillion.

If SpaceX bought Tesla at those values, Musk would own about 37% of the combined company and control 56% of the vote, Levy said. That's well above the 25% Tesla stake he has long said he wants.

That's why Barclays expects SpaceX to be the buyer in an all-stock deal. At current values, each Tesla share would be worth about 0.7 SpaceX shares before any takeover premium.

But the biggest factor weighing in favor of a merger happening is that Musk himself has heavily hinted at a tie-up of his two biggest companies.

On Tesla's latest earnings call, Musk noted that there's "more and more overlap" between his two companies, whether it's operations, technology, or even SpaceX buying Tesla Cybertrucks. There are also Musk's own remarks at the All-In Summit last month.

"With all this collaboration, on so many levels, who can imagine what action one might take when there's so much close collaboration in so many areas," he said.

articles.title: Apple iPhone Duo available for preorder Friday
articles.summary: Apple's iPhone Duo is available for preorder Friday, Oct. 16.
articles.body:
Apple's ( AAPL ) foldable iPhone Duo is up for preorder on Friday, just days after the company's market cap topped $5 trillion for the second time .

Apple's most ambitious iPhone yet, the passport-sized Duo is also one of Apple's priciest smartphones to date.

Starting at $1,999, the Duo features a 5.4-inch front display and a 7.6-inch foldable inner screen, with a nano-texture finish that helps prevent glare while making the panel's center crease all but invisible.

The book-style foldable is a first for Apple, which has sat out the folding-phone market for years while rivals Samsung ( 005930.KS ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) have grabbed market share and iterated on their designs.

But Apple is notorious for allowing other companies to do the legwork in developing a new market only to swoop in and grab its own piece of the pie. That's exactly what the iPhone maker did with the AirPods and Apple Watch, which have become bestselling devices in their respective categories.

The iPhone Duo brings a number of new features to Apple's all-important product line, including the ability to run two apps side by side or two windows of the same app simultaneously.

Apps seamlessly transition from the front screen to the main display and back. You can also take advantage of the Duo's foldable design by positioning it like an open laptop on your desk, allowing you to view content on the top of the screen while navigating on the bottom half.

In Standing Mode, you can position the Duo like a tent on a flat surface to watch shows and movies, or use the phone as a high-powered clock for your nightstand.

Apple has also thrown in some extras on the camera front. If you unfold the phone and open the camera app, the front screen will provide your subject with a preview of your shot. The idea is to spare friends, couples, and everyone in between the awful experience of having someone take your picture, only to immediately look at the result and demand a redo.

The Duo gets ultra-wide-angle and wide-angle rear cameras, but no telephoto option. Up front, the phone gets Apple's Center Stage camera, which helps keep the user in view even if they move side to side.

There's also an under-display FaceTime camera hidden beneath the main folding screen.

Foldable phones are still a relatively niche market segment. According to market research firm IDC , manufacturers were projected to ship 1.25 billion units in 2025. Foldables were expected to make up just 20.6 million of those.

But the company says it anticipates foldable smartphones will account for roughly 10% of the market by 2029. It hit a major cumulative milestone in 2026 with total lifetime units set to surpass 100 million by the end of the year, according to Counterpoint Research's latest Foldable Smartphone Market Forecast .

articles.title: Sylvester Stallone on AI in Hollywood: 'It makes things so much easier'
articles.summary: Sylvester Stallone talks about how AI could tell the backstory of his iconic John Rambo character.
articles.body:
Listen and subscribe to Power Players with Brian Sozzi on Apple Podcasts , Amazon Music , Spotify , YouTube , or wherever you find your favorite podcasts.

Maybe John Rambo wasn't always a one-man killing machine.

AI can help tell that story, and perhaps one day soon it will, says the living, breathing soul of John Rambo: Sylvester Stallone.

"If Harrison Ford, myself, or another actor wanted to do the prequel — like how did this guy get so screwed up, like in Rambo. You have AI now, which they tested, and they take me to 18 years old, when he was happy-go-lucky, he was captain of the team, he was the most popular person in school. He joined the army because he thought this would be fun for two weeks. And then you see the metamorphosis on how his soul was torn out of his body. That stuff is fascinating," Stallone said in a new episode of the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast (video above; listen in below).

The use of AI remains a hot-button issue in the Hollywood creative community amid fears that it will lead to job losses. The reality is that AI is already being used, and on some big movie projects.

Iconic actors from Stallone's generation, including Joe Pesci and Al Pacino, alongside Robert De Niro, were extensively de-aged using AI-driven visual effects software in Martin Scorsese's "The Irishman" to portray their characters across several decades.

More recently, Harrison Ford was transformed into a 1980s-era Indiana Jones for an opening sequence in "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny." Lucasfilm used algorithms trained on decades of archived footage.

"Every other person in the movie is real. They are just doing one character," Stallone said. "I said, wow, that would be interesting. There are so many characters [to explore], like how did he get so crazy? How did he become this? Now you would understand the evolution. That is something I am working on."

The non-AI Stallone has earned his spot among Hollywood legends through blood, sweat, and tears.

With that success — ranging from big-screen films "Rocky" and "Rambo" to the series "Tulsa King," which returns for its latest season on Friday on streaming platform Paramount+ — has come an equally impressive business backdrop despite not owning the rights to "Rocky."

Recognizing the power of controlling his own IP, Stallone expanded his earnings beyond simple acting fees — which routinely topped $15 million to $20 million per project — by taking on writer, director, and executive producer roles across his iconic "Rocky," "Rambo," and "The Expendables" franchises.

Mortgage rates were unchanged on the week despite daily bond market fluctuations and new data that showed inflation is still running hot.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.4% for the week through Wednesday, according to Freddie Mac data, holding steady at the highest levels since late 2023.

The rate stability masked some daily bond market fluctuations. On Wednesday, new data showed that inflation was a hotter-than-expected 3.7% in September . The 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates closely track, initially jumped on the news, before retreating later in the day amid growing consensus that the Federal Reserve will still opt to hold rates steady at its meeting later this month and raise them in December.

The Fed doesn't directly control mortgage rates, but its interest rate decisions do influence their direction.

"Mortgage rates are unlikely to ease anytime soon, but bringing inflation under control would pave the way for lower rates and a much-needed boost to affordability for the year ahead," Realtor.com Senior Economist Jiayi Xu said in a statement.

Some rate relief, however, could be around the corner in the days ahead, courtesy of the bond market. The 10-year yield plunged nearly 10 basis points to 5.1% on Thursday as jittery investors sought safe-haven bond investments amid a rout in tech stocks.
